decisions.rationale: Lead Pelipper and Swampert to immediately set Rain via Drizzle and trigger Swift Swim on Mega Swampert for immense offensive pressure. Back Basculegion and Archaludon as potent cleaning and defensive options.
decisions.notebook: Drizzle rain core with Pelipper + Mega Swampert lead, backed by Basculegion and Archaludon. Strong vs Whimsicott/Gholdengo/Blastoise/Ninetales core.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott plus Gholdengo establishes immediate priority Sunny Day disruption against Pelipper rain and prevents Swift Swim from dictating the game, while Gholdengo pressures common rain leads and ignores Fake Out. Mega Blastoise adds strong special coverage and Tauros-Blaze threatens Archaludon and Tsareena with Close Combat and sun-boosted Fire attacks.
decisions.notebook: Preferred Game 1 composition is Whimsicott/Gholdengo lead with Mega Blastoise and Tauros-Blaze in reserve. Prioritize Prankster Sunny Day against Pelipper rain; Tailwind is the alternate speed-control line. Gholdengo is protected from opposing status by Good as Gold and from Fake Out by its Ghost typing. Tauros is the main answer to Archaludon and Tsareena; Mega Blastoise supplies bulky special coverage, though Water Spout is weakened in sun.

decisions.rationale: Tailwind sets up speed control for our team. Swampert Mega Evolves and uses Waterfall on Gholdengo to deal massive damage in rain, threatening a heavy hit or KO on Gholdengo while Pelipper secures Tailwind.
decisions.notebook: Pelipper + Swampert rain core standard opening. Tailwind enables swift play under rain.

decisions.rationale: Pelipper fainted, so we bring in Basculegion to clean up with Adaptive Wave Crash under rain or outspeed under Choice Scarf. Swampert-Mega holds position and protects or attacks while Basculegion enters.
decisions.notebook: Pelipper + Swampert rain core standard opening. Tailwind enables swift play under rain. Basculegion and Archaludon in reserve.

selection: Sunny Day (all adjacent, including ally Gholdengo)
decisions.rationale: Prankster Sunny Day removes Rain and prevents Mega Swampert from exploiting Swift Swim, while weakening opposing Water attacks. Gholdengo’s Thunderbolt is 4× super effective into Pelipper and is a guaranteed OHKO, immediately eliminating its weather and Tailwind support.
decisions.notebook: Preferred Game 1 plan remains Whimsicott/Gholdengo lead with Prankster Sunny Day against Pelipper rain. Gholdengo can reliably remove Pelipper with Thunderbolt. Preserve Mega Blastoise and Tauros-Blaze for later; Tauros is the primary answer to Archaludon and Tsareena, while Mega Blastoise provides bulky special coverage.

decisions.rationale: Basculegion outspeeds Gholdengo and hits it with Last Respects (super-effective), while Mega Swampert uses Earthquake to hit Gholdengo super-effectively and deal damage to Whimsicott.

Encore Swampert-Mega’s revealed Waterfall, preventing Earthquake while Gholdengo Protects against Basculegion’s dangerous attack. This preserves both Pokémon, blocks the strongest spread threat, and creates a safer position to target Basculegion next turn.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 plan: preserve Mega Blastoise and Tauros-Paldea-Blaze for the midgame. Tauros is the primary answer to Archaludon and Tsareena; Mega Blastoise supplies bulky special coverage. Against rain teams, prioritize early weather control with Whimsicott and preserve Gholdengo when possible. Track revealed moves, items, abilities, and opposing speed ranges across games.

Mega Swampert is Adamant with Waterfall, Earthquake, Ice Punch, Protect, and is vulnerable to continued Encore pressure. Opponent’s remaining unrevealed possibilities are Archaludon, Raichu, or Tsareena; only one is present alongside the three revealed foes. Against rain, prioritize Whimsicott weather control and preserve Gholdengo when practical.

decisions.rationale: Encore Swampert to keep it locked into Waterfall while Gholdengo pressures Archaludon with super-effective Shadow Ball; this preserves control and avoids the weak spread damage of Make It Rain.
decisions.notebook: Mega Swampert is Adamant, carries Waterfall, Earthquake, Ice Punch, and Protect, and can be kept under Encore pressure. Basculegion was Choice Scarf Adamant Adaptability and was locked into Last Respects. Preserve Mega Blastoise and Tauros-Paldea-Blaze for the midgame; Tauros is the main Archaludon/Tsareena answer, while Mega Blastoise supplies bulky special coverage. Against rain, prioritize Whimsicott weather control and preserve Gholdengo when practical.

decisions.rationale: Bring in Tauros to apply Intimidate and use its superior Speed and Fighting pressure against weakened Archaludon while preserving Mega Blastoise for the midgame. Gholdengo passes to avoid unnecessary exposure while Tauros handles the immediate threat.

Archaludon is Modest with Stamina, Electro Shot, Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, and Iron Defense. Preserve Mega Blastoise and Tauros for the midgame; Tauros is the primary Archaludon/Tsareena answer, while Mega Blastoise provides bulky special coverage. Against rain, prioritize weather control and preserve Gholdengo when practical.

decisions.rationale: Swampert uses Protect to shield against Tauros/Gholdengo threats while Archaludon releases its charged Electro Shot into Gholdengo.
decisions.notebook: Swampert and Archaludon are strong pivots. Protect + Electro Shot stabilizes turn 5.

decisions.rationale: Tauros uses Close Combat to guarantee the KO on Archaludon before Electro Shot releases. Gholdengo Protects to avoid Swampert’s spread Earthquake, preserving both attackers while Tauros absorbs the reduced damage and leaves a favorable 2v1.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mega Blastoise for midgame as bulky special coverage and weather control. Tauros-Paldea-Blaze is the primary answer to Archaludon and Tsareena; use its Fighting pressure to remove Steel threats. Preserve Gholdengo when practical against rain teams, using Protect to avoid spread Ground pressure. Maintain weather control and prioritize denying charged Electro Shot when possible.

decisions.rationale: Waterfall hits Tauros for super-effective damage while Gholdengo is vulnerable, avoiding hitting our fainted ally with Earthquake.
decisions.notebook: Swampert-Mega is the last remaining Pokémon. Tauros and Gholdengo are active.

decisions.rationale: Both attacks resolve before Swampert across its full Speed range. Close Combat is Tauros’s strongest neutral option, while Shadow Ball is Gholdengo’s best pressure; together they can potentially finish Swampert before its spread Ground attack, unlike the resisted alternatives. Preserve Mega Blastoise for later.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mega Blastoise for midgame as bulky special coverage and weather control. Tauros is the primary answer to Steel threats and should retain Fighting pressure. Preserve Gholdengo when practical against spread Ground pressure, but prioritize immediate removal of dangerous charged or boosted threats. Maintain weather control against rain teams.

decisions.notebook: Swampert-Mega is the last remaining Pokémon. Game 1 lost.

decisions.rationale: Blastoise Protects while Gholdengo uses its faster Shadow Ball to finish the 21% Swampert-Mega. Mega Evolution is unnecessary because Blastoise is not attacking, preserving the stone and avoiding needless commitment.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mega Blastoise for situations requiring its boosted coverage or weather control; avoid Mega Evolution when a teammate can safely secure the immediate KO. Gholdengo remains valuable against spread Ground pressure, but its faster Shadow Ball is the reliable finisher against weakened Swampert-Mega.

decisions.rationale: Swampert-Mega is at 21% HP after Protect last turn. Gholdengo and Blastoise are both on the field. Earthquake hits both opponents at -1 attack. None of the single-target moves can break through Gholdengo or Blastoise while avoiding taking a KO. Game 1 is effectively lost, so we fight to the end with Earthquake.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 lost. Swampert-Mega is the last mon. Gholdengo and Blastoise present.

decisions.rationale: Gholdengo moves before Swampert and Shadow Ball guarantees the KO at 21%. Blastoise remains un-Mega-Evolved and uses full-power Water Spout, also guaranteeing the KO if Swampert does not Protect; Mega Evolution is unnecessary and preserving it retains future boosted coverage.
decisions.notebook: Preserve Mega Blastoise for situations requiring boosted coverage or weather control; avoid Mega Evolution when a teammate can safely secure the immediate KO. Gholdengo's faster Shadow Ball is a reliable finisher against weakened Swampert-Mega. Prioritize coordinated doubles decisions and retain Gholdengo when spread Ground pressure is a concern.

reflections.summary: The opponent neutralized our weather advantage immediately with Sunny Day via Whimsicott and disrupted our positioning with Encore, while Gholdengo and Tauros dismantled our offensive threats. Bringing Pelipper into a Whimsicott/Gholdengo lead allowed Whimsicott to overwrite the rain and Gholdengo to pick off Pelipper on turn 1, leaving Swampert-Mega and Basculegion unable to break through the defensive answers.
reflections.adjustment: Consider bringing Archaludon or a more resilient lead alongside Swampert-Mega to handle Whimsicott's weather-setting and Prankster utility without forfeiting early momentum to Gholdengo.
reflections.notebook: Opponent uses Whimsicott (Focus Sash, Sunny Day, Tailwind, Encore, Moonblast), Gholdengo (Leftovers, Make It Rain, Shadow Ball, Thunderbolt, Protect), Blastoise (Blastoisinite, Water Spout, Aura Sphere, Ice Beam, Protect), and Tauros-Paldea-Blaze (Expert Belt, Close Combat, Raging Bull, Flare Blitz, Protect). Whimsicott counters rain immediately via Sunny Day. Gholdengo possesses Leftovers recovery and Good as Gold. Blastoise carries Blastoisinite. Maushold and Alolan Ninetales were not brought Game 1.

reflections.summary: Won because the brought four matched the rain offense: Whimsicott reversed Pelipper’s weather and disrupted Mega Swampert, while Gholdengo safely removed the vulnerable Water/Ghost threats. Blastoise was a suitable non-Mega reserve; evolving it was unnecessary because Gholdengo and Tauros secured the key KOs.
reflections.adjustment: Keep the anti-rain core, but consider bringing Tsareena over Tauros next game: Power Whip pressures Mega Swampert and Queenly Majesty limits Aqua Jet, reducing reliance on Intimidate and Close Combat drops. Continue withholding Mega Evolution unless Mega Blastoise’s boosted coverage is needed immediately.
reflections.notebook: Opponent’s rain mode uses Damp Rock Pelipper with Rain Dance, Tailwind, and Wide Guard; Sunny Day is a strong reversal and should remain a priority. Mega Swampert is an Adamant physical attacker with Waterfall, Ice Punch, Earthquake, and Protect, while Choice Scarf Adaptability Basculegion can threaten immediate Last Respects pressure. Archaludon may use Electro Shot and Iron Defense, so deny setup or remove it quickly. Gholdengo is a reliable answer to the rain core and should be preserved against spread Ground pressure. Reassess Tsareena over Tauros for Swampert pressure and priority control; Mega Blastoise need not evolve unless its boosted coverage is required.
